---
title: "How far does it glide when hand-launched from a standing throw?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 90.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 200.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 38.6      # s the probe actually used

import aerosandbox as asb

plane = get_airplane()
mass, cg = get_mass_properties(plane)
weight = mass * 9.81

opti = asb.Opti()
alpha = opti.variable(init_guess=6.0, lower_bound=-5.0, upper_bound=15.0)
velocity = opti.variable(init_guess=5.0, lower_bound=1.0, upper_bound=20.0)

op_point = asb.OperatingPoint(
    velocity=velocity,
    alpha=alpha
)

aero = asb.AeroBuildup(
    airplane=plane,
    op_point=op_point
).run()

opti.subject_to(aero["L"] == weight)
opti.minimize(aero["D"])

sol = opti.solve(verbose=False)
max_LD = sol.value(aero["L"]) / sol.value(aero["D"])

launch_height = 1.5
glide_distance = launch_height * max_LD
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{glide_distance:.1f} m"`]{.hero-value}
[glide distance from shoulder height]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** From a typical standing throw, the aircraft glides approximately [`{python} f"{glide_distance:.1f}"`]{.key} meters. This assumes a release from [`{python} f"{launch_height:.1f}"`]{.key} m and an optimal launch that immediately achieves steady flight at its maximum lift-to-drag ratio of [`{python} f"{max_LD:.2f}"`]{.key}.

::: {.callout-note}
## New assumptions
1. **launch height: 1.5 m**, shoulder height for standing throw.
:::
